messages:
monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: PROD /paging-orch 5xx spike - 50 errors in 2m, error_code=upstream_503, request_id=rcpt-9f3a
maya.sre: saw this, did we get pages?
alex.eng: i haven't received any pages, my phone was quiet
incident-bot: automatic page suppressed: downstream-pager returned 429 (rate_limit) for integration=pager-proxy, suppression_policy=exponential_backoff
maya.sre: ugh, so the incident bot is intentionally suppressing because pager-proxy is throttling?
jamie: looking at webhook-queue metrics now, queue length ~ 12k, processing latency ~ 5s -> worker errors showing 503 from pager-proxy
alex.eng: can someone run: `kubectl -n infra logs deployment/paging-webhook -f --since=1m | grep 429 | head`
jamie: pasted short logs:
```
2026-03-18T14:45:02Z WARN send_page failed status=429 body="rate limited"
2026-03-18T14:45:05Z ERROR retrying page id=rcpt-9f3a attempts=3
2026-03-18T14:45:08Z ERROR downstream 503 for provider=pager-proxy
```
alex.eng: thanks. Looks like pager-proxy is intermittently returning 503/429 which triggers incident-bot suppression. That explains missed phone pages.
ops-bot: we've got ongoing customer impact: two customers reported missed alerts (CS ticket #2314), investigating severity
maya.sre: manual escalation: @alex.eng can you trigger manual SMS to oncall? i'm oncall but didn't get page
alex.eng: manually paged maya.sre via provider UI, pls confirm\maya.sre: got it — phone ringing now, thanks.
jamie: quick mitigation options: 1) increase webhook worker concurrency to drain queue (temp), 2) disable incident-bot auto-suppression for pager-proxy integration, 3) failover to secondary pager provider (needs config + keys)
alex.eng: doing option 1 now: `kubectl -n infra scale deployment/paging-webhook --replicas=6`
incident-bot: config check: suppression_policy for pager-proxy = enabled, grace_window=30s, max_backoff=10m
jamie: scaling applied, worker pods coming up (3 -> 6), Q length dropping to ~3k
ops-bot: customer impact update: CS confirmed 2 missed pages in last 10m, no active outages reported by customers yet, marking P1 candidate until resolved
maya.sre: can we temporarily disable suppression? we should avoid the bot silently skipping pages while provider struggles
alex.eng: toggled suppression=false for integration=pager-proxy in vault (apply in 10s)
incident-bot: warning: suppression policy changed by alex.eng, new_state=disabled
jamie: provider is still returning 503s but with suppression off we see retries; queue continues to drain, errors tapering
ops-bot: CS: outreach done to affected accounts, they escalated but okay with follow-up postmortem
maya.sre: confirmed phone alerts resumed and we have an ack from oncall
alex.eng: rolling restart of webhook-worker to pick new config: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/paging-webhook`
jamie: follow-up: file shows pager-proxy hitting their rate-limiting due to burst; talking to vendor but we should add local client-side token-bucket smoothing and a failover provider in case of provider-side rate-limits
maya.sre: thanks all — please add these action items to the incident ticket. Good job on manual escalation. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident ticket INC-2026-0318 created, severity=P2 -> will update to P1 if further customer impact occurs
alex.eng: logging notes for postmortem: triggered by upstream 503s -> bot suppression hid retries -> manual paging needed -> mitigation: disable suppression + scale workers -> recovered.
jamie: i'll open a PR to add: (a) failover provider config, (b) automations to alert when suppression blocks >1 page/min, (c) smoothing token-bucket on webhook client
maya.sre: add an oncall runbook step to alert Slack channel if pages suppressed and no oncall ack within 1m
alex.eng: thanks, everyone. I'll follow up with vendor thread and the postmortem draft later today.
incident-bot: incident resolved? awaiting final owner confirmation
maya.sre: i consider this mitigated. closing thread after postmortem.
